solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Choose the French preserves to have with meals (7)

annotation.surface: A diner is told to select the French jars of relish to go with dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The French' is a standard way to ask for LE, LA or LES; the answer's length tells you which.
annotation.definitionFit: Pickles are vegetables preserved in vinegar and served alongside a meal.

entries.clue: Elders of church arranging best prayers — ace output! (10)

indicatorNotes.arranging: the letters are put in a new order
indicatorNotes.output: the A (ace) is put out of the fodder

blocks.note: A = ace, as on a playing card; remove it to leave BESTPRYERS

annotation.surface: Church elders are organising the finest prayers, with an exclamation at their productivity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Output' reads as a noun praising the elders' work; split it as 'out put' and it tells you to throw the ace (A) out before rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: Presbyters are elders in the early Christian or Presbyterian church.

entries.clue: Mark and maiden in state of unconsciousness (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the maiden inside the state of unconsciousness, so COMA wraps round the M

blocks.note: a coma is a state of unconsciousness
M = maiden, a cricket over with no runs scored

annotation.surface: A mark and a young woman are found out cold together.
annotation.walkthrough: M for maiden comes from cricket scorecards, where a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored.
annotation.definitionFit: Mark here means punctuation mark, and the comma is the commonest one.

entries.clue: Something alcoholic, something very cold and sweet (9)

annotation.surface: A drinks order: a spirit, some ice, and something sugary.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a list of three things, so 'and sweet' looks like a third item rather than the definition. Liquorice is the British spelling of licorice.
annotation.definitionFit: Liquorice is a chewy black sweet (candy) flavoured with the root of the liquorice plant.

entries.clue: Tolerates provision for spectators at matches (6)

blocks.note: she can't stand him = she can't tolerate him
the tiered seating built round a sports ground for the crowd

annotation.surface: Someone puts up with the seating laid on for fans at games.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves are the same word in different senses: a verb, then a plural noun.
annotation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate it; stands are the tiered seating at a ground.

entries.clue: Fellow in short section of book (4)

indicatorNotes.short: the word is cut down to its opening letters

blocks.note: a section of a book is a chapter; 'short' asks for its standard abbreviation, the first four letters

annotation.surface: A man is sitting in a brief part of a novel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chap' is British for a man or fellow; the wordplay is CHAPTER trimmed to its standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A chap is an informal British word for a man, a fellow.

entries.clue: Vehicle is endless worry (3)

indicatorNotes.endless: the last letter is taken off

annotation.surface: Owning a motor is a constant source of anxiety.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Endless' in the surface means never-ending; in the wordplay it means the end is cut off.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the car is the everyday motor vehicle on any road.

entries.clue: Word of prayer associated with the German reformer? (7)

annotation.surface: A prayer word tied to the German reformer, which suggests Martin Luther.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The German reformer' conjures Luther, but 'the German' is just DER and 'reformer' alone is the definition: one who amends. The question mark flags the trick.
annotation.definitionFit: An amender is someone who amends, that is, reforms or corrects something.

entries.clue: Bedlam when odd characters get lost in wood (3)

indicatorNotes.odd characters get lost: the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters are dropped, keeping the even ones

annotation.surface: Chaos breaks out when some eccentric people wander off into the woods.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' reads as eccentric people getting lost in a forest; in the wordplay they are the odd-numbered letters of Bedlam.
annotation.definitionFit: Wood by example: elm is a hardwood timber, and wood can mean a kind of timber as well as a forest.

entries.clue: A squire frenziedly crossing river hunted animals (8)

indicatorNotes.frenziedly: the letters are thrown into wild disorder
indicatorNotes.crossing: the anagram goes across, around, the R

annotation.surface: A country squire races wildly over a river in pursuit of game.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a hunting scene, so 'hunted animals' at the end sits naturally; the anagram of A SQUIRE is wrapped round R.
annotation.definitionFit: A quarry is an animal being hunted; quarries is the plural.

entries.clue: Maybe crab and tuna, scarce at sea (10)

annotation.surface: Crab and tuna are both hard to find in the ocean these days.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crab and tuna' looks like a pair of seafood; the definition stops at 'crab', with 'maybe' saying crab is one example, and the tuna joins the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A crab is one kind of crustacean, so 'maybe crab' is a crustacean.

entries.clue: Jolly good supporter, very old (5)

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting garment

annotation.surface: A cheer for a loyal fan who has been following the team for ages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan; in crosswords it is often a bra.
annotation.definitionFit: Bravo is an exclamation of approval, the same as 'Jolly good!'

entries.clue: Crucial point editor put about alcoholic drink (7)

indicatorNotes.put about: to put a ship about is to turn it round, so ED turns to DE

blocks.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

annotation.surface: At the key moment, the editor spread word about someone's drinking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put about' looks like spreading a rumour, but it is a sailing term for turning round. A decider is the final game that settles a tied contest.
annotation.definitionFit: A decider is the deciding game or moment, the crucial point of a contest.

entries.clue: Conservative girl I term “mostly traditional”? (9)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word is kept, dropping the last letter

blocks.note: C = Conservative, the UK political party
to term is to call, as in 'we call it'; 'mostly' then drops the final L

annotation.surface: A conservative girl describes herself as more or less old-fashioned.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'mostly traditional' look like a phrase the girl uses; in fact 'mostly' works on 'term', and 'traditional' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Classical means traditional and long established, as in classical style.

entries.clue: Understand fool (4,2)

blocks.note: to grasp or absorb what you are told
to be taken in is to be fooled

annotation.walkthrough: 'Fool' could be a noun, but here it is a verb, matching the verb 'understand'.
annotation.definitionFit: Take in means both to grasp and to deceive.

entries.clue: Most compassionate type, English saint (7)

blocks.note: a kind is a type or sort

annotation.surface: An English saint is described as the most compassionate sort of person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Type' reads as 'sort of person' in the surface, but it is the noun KIND.
annotation.definitionFit: Kindest is the superlative of kind, meaning most compassionate.

entries.clue: Sign he’s not found in Roget’s reference book? (6)

indicatorNotes.not found in: HES is removed from inside the word

blocks.note: Roget's Thesaurus is the famous book of synonyms
the letters of he's, removed from THESAURUS

annotation.surface: Some word or symbol that does not appear in Roget's famous reference work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like any sign, but it is a sign of the zodiac. Take HES out of T(HES)AURUS.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-favourite sense: sign means star sign, and the bull is the second of the twelve.

entries.clue: Making request in the role of monarch (6)

blocks.note: as = in the role of, e.g. 'acting as chairman'

annotation.surface: Someone petitions the throne while playing the part of a king.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the role of' is a common way to clue AS, as in 'acting as chairman'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to ask is to make a request, and the -ing form matches 'making'.

entries.clue: Illegal players? They know the ropes (7)

blocks.note: a ringer is a competitor fraudulently entered under another's name
in a church tower, the people who pull the bell ropes know them literally

annotation.surface: Cheats in a team are old hands who know all the tricks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Know the ropes' is an idiom for being experienced; bell-ringers know them literally.
annotation.definitionFit: Ringers are both illicit substitutes in a game and people who ring church bells.

entries.clue: Sarah’s leading a dance (5)

indicatorNotes.leading: 'leading' means going in front, so Sarah's name sits ahead of the A

blocks.note: Sal is a short form of Sarah; add the 's

annotation.surface: Sarah is in front, leading the others in a dance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sarah's leading' looks like 'Sarah is leading'; it is Sal's, placed first.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: salsa is one Latin American dance, danced to Cuban and Puerto Rican music.

entries.clue: Torch, say, not hard to carry (5)

blocks.note: in Britain a torch is a flashlight, one kind of lamp; 'say' marks it as an example

annotation.surface: A torch is easy to carry about.
annotation.walkthrough: In British English a torch is a flashlight; 'say' marks it as one example of a light.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: a torch is one example of a lamp, and a load that is easy to carry weighs little.

entries.clue: Dreadful comedian is possessed by the devil? (8)

indicatorNotes.Dreadful: the letters are in a dreadful state, jumbled

annotation.surface: A comic is so bad on stage he must be in the grip of Satan.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a critic's joke about a terrible comic; the question mark admits the exaggeration.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word describes someone in the grip of a demon, and serves as an adjective as well as a noun.

entries.clue: Part of regalia held by senior bishop (3)

indicatorNotes.held by: the answer is held inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the last two letters of senior and the first of bishop

annotation.surface: A piece of the crown jewels is carried by a high-ranking bishop at a coronation.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface fits a coronation, where bishops do handle the regalia, so the hidden ORB is in the scene too.
annotation.definitionFit: The orb, a jewelled globe topped with a cross, is part of the royal regalia.

entries.clue: Some strange episode? Gosh! (3)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters are taken, from inside the phrase

blocks.note: the last two letters of strange and the first of episode

annotation.surface: Someone reacts in surprise to an odd event.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark belongs to the definition: gee and gosh are both mild exclamations.
annotation.definitionFit: Gee is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh.

entries.clue: Try turning creatures of the night back (4)

indicatorNotes.turning: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the letters run in reverse
indicatorNotes.back: 'back' means backwards, so the letters are read from the end to the start

annotation.surface: An attempt to drive off nocturnal animals.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'stab' at something is an attempt at it, so 'try' is a noun here.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'have a go at' and 'have a try at' share their noun with this one, an attempt.

entries.clue: Setter atingle with excitement (7)

annotation.surface: The crossword setter is thrilled and tingling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword setter; it is something that makes a liquid set, as gelatin sets a jelly.
annotation.definitionFit: Gelatin is used to set jellies and desserts, so it is a setter.
